featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kyani & Co. is a classic Iranian café serving authentic Iranian cuisine. The place is always crowded, and you’ll notice a good mix of locals and foreigners, which shows how popular and well-known it is.

Coming to the food, their chicken dishes stood out. The Chicken Cheese Kebab was actually very nice—it was stuffed with cheese from inside and had a hot-dog–like shape. It felt filling and had a good amount of chicken, which I liked the most.

I also tried the chicken samosa, but I felt the chicken quantity was a bit less, with more masala in the filling. Similarly, the mutton cutlet had more potato than mutton. Personally, I prefer meat-forward dishes.

The ambience is really great with an old-world charm, but photography is not allowed inside. I clicked one photo and was asked not to take pictures, which was a bit disappointing considering how beautiful the place is.

Overall, it’s an authentic Iranian café with a lovely atmosphere. The food is good, especially the chicken items, though the filling ratios may not suit everyone’s taste.

featured_reviews.name: Viraj Redkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Kyani & Co. and honestly, it felt less like a café visit and more like a journey back in time. The moment you walk in, the old-world charm hits you — vintage wooden furniture, classic tiled floors, and an atmosphere that carries stories from over 100 years ago. It’s raw, real, and beautifully untouched.
We ordered the iconic Irani chai, bun maska, and kheema pav — and every bite was pure nostalgia. The chai had that perfect strong, comforting flavor, the bun maska was soft with just the right amount of buttery goodness, and the kheema pav was rich, flavorful, and absolutely satisfying.
What makes this place special isn’t just the food — it’s the experience. No fancy frills, no modern distractions, just timeless simplicity done right.
A small heads-up: it’s strictly cash only — no cards, no UPI — which somehow adds to its old-school vibe.
If you’re in Mumbai and want to experience something authentic, soulful, and truly fascinating, this place is not just a café… it’s a legacy you can taste.

featured_reviews.name: Stringzzz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya – A Timeless Taste of Authentic Gujarati Thali

Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is one of the most iconic and beloved places to experience authentic Gujarati cuisine. Known for its traditional thali, warm hospitality, and consistent quality, this legendary eatery has earned a special place in the hearts of locals as well as visitors. Dining here feels less like eating at a restaurant and more like being welcomed into a Gujarati household.

The moment you enter Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya, you are greeted with simplicity and warmth. The interiors are modest, clean, and functional, reflecting the traditional values of Gujarati culture where food quality and hospitality matter more than luxury décor. The seating arrangement is organized, and despite the heavy rush during peak hours, the staff manages the crowd efficiently.

The highlight, without any doubt, is the Gujarati Thali. The thali is a wholesome and balanced meal that represents the true essence of Gujarat’s culinary heritage. It usually includes a variety of rotating dishes such as shaak (vegetable curries), kadhi, dal, rotli or puri, rice, khichdi, farsan, chutneys, pickles, and traditional sweets like shrikhand or mohanthal. Each item is freshly prepared and served hot.

One of the most impressive aspects of Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is the unlimited serving system. The staff continuously serves food with great attentiveness, ensuring that guests never feel rushed or restricted. The flavors are authentic—mildly spiced, well-balanced, and comforting—making the food suitable for all age groups. The use of fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods is clearly reflected in the taste.

Historically, Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya has been serving Gujarati food for decades and is considered a cultural landmark. It has preserved the original style of Gujarati dining, where meals are meant to nourish both the body and the soul. Many regular visitors associate the place with nostalgia, family gatherings, and cultural pride.

Cleanliness and hygiene are well maintained throughout the restaurant. Plates, serving areas, and dining spaces are kept tidy, even during peak hours. The staff is polite, disciplined, and well trained, adding to the overall pleasant dining experience.

The pricing is reasonable, especially considering the quality, quantity, and authenticity of the food served. It offers excellent value for money and is often recommended as a must-visit place for anyone wanting to experience true Gujarati cuisine.

Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya attracts a diverse crowd—families, elderly guests, tourists, and food lovers from across India. Despite the popularity and long waiting times during weekends, the management ensures smooth operations and quick table turnover without compromising service quality.

Overall, Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is not just a restaurant but a celebration of Gujarati tradition, flavors, and hospitality. If you want to experience a soulful Gujarati thali prepared with authenticity and served with warmth, this place is an absolute must-visit. It leaves you with a satisfied heart, a happy stomach, and a deep appreciation for Gujarat’s rich culinary culture.

featured_reviews.review_text: This unassuming spot might just serve some of the best fried prawns in the city. The prawns are succulent and perfectly cooked, encased in a crisp, red coloured batter that achieves just the right balance of texture and flavour. The accompanying green chutney is a standout, adding a zesty punch that elevates the dish to another level. At Rs. 234 for a modest 150g portion, it’s not exactly a budget option, but the quality makes it a fair deal. These prawns would pair beautifully with a chilled beverage of your choice if you’re planning a casual meal at home. That said, there’s a certain charm in enjoying them right there, standing on the street. The service is quick, making it a convenient stop before catching a movie at the nearby Metro Theatre. Whether you’re in the mood for fried fish, chicken, prawns, or Pomfret, this spot delivers a consistently satisfying, indulgent experience—a classic that’s earned its reputation in the area.

Visited Mahesh Lunch Home and had a wonderful dining experience. We tried the Butter Garlic Prawns, Crab Lollipop, Jumbo Tawa Prawns, and Chicken Biryani. The seafood was fresh, perfectly cooked, and packed with flavor. The Butter Garlic Prawns were rich and delicious, while the Jumbo Tawa Prawns stood out with their excellent seasoning. The Crab Lollipop was crispy and enjoyable, and the Chicken Biryani was aromatic and satisfying.

A special mention for their Solkadi, which is always on the darker side. While it has a distinctive flavor, I feel a slightly lighter preparation could bring more subtlety and balance, making it even more refreshing and enjoyable to sip alongside the seafood.

The service was attentive, and the overall ambiance made for a great meal. Definitely a place worth visiting for seafood lovers. Highly recommended!

The Chicken Chettinad was amazing—rich, aromatic, and authentic, with a well-rounded masala that really stood out. The squid was also quite tasty, fresh, and cooked just right.

The place itself has a nice ambience, is clean and hygienic, and the overall quality of food is clearly well maintained. The staff are very friendly, polite, and attentive, which adds positively to the experience.

While the prices are on the higher side, the quality, hygiene, and taste justify the cost. A good place for quality food and a relaxed dining experience—definitely worth a visit. Only issue is Parking. Better to go in a taxi.

Mahesh Lunch Lounge was an absolute standout and easily one of our best meals in India. We chose to eat here over the Taj after it was strongly recommended by locals — and we are so glad we listened. From start to finish, the experience was fantastic.

The food was exceptional, especially the seafood. The tiger prawns were MASSIVE — genuinely some of the biggest prawns we’ve ever seen, let alone eaten. They were cooked perfectly, full of flavour, and without doubt the best prawns we had in India. That’s saying something, especially as we truly believed Kerala couldn’t be beaten when it came to seafood.

Service was attentive and efficient without being overbearing, and the prices were surprisingly good for the quality and portion sizes. One bit of advice: order your starters before committing to mains — the portions are generous and we definitely over-ordered because everything sounded too good to miss (no regrets, just very full 😅).

Overall, Mahesh Lunch Lounge completely lived up to the hype and then some. Incredible food, huge portions, great service, and excellent value. If you’re debating where to eat — go here.

I ordered the pav bhaji and chole bhature, and both were outstanding. The pav bhaji was rich, buttery, and perfectly spiced with that authentic street-style flavor, yet it felt clean and hygienic. The chole bhature was just as impressive — fluffy, hot bhature paired with chole that had deep, balanced masala without being overly oily. You could taste the freshness in every bite.

What really elevated the experience was the staff. I was new to Mumbai and a bit overwhelmed, but they were incredibly friendly and patient. They took the time to explain the menu, recommend what to try, and even shared how each dish is traditionally eaten. At no point did I feel rushed despite the constant crowd outside.

I also noticed how neat and well-maintained the place was. For a busy street-side eatery, the tables were clean, the serving area was organized, and the staff did not feel rushed.

Great food, warm service, and surprising neatness in the heart of Mumbai’s bustle. I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended if you want authentic flavors without compromising on hygiene

They had a delightful tandoori coating, and the filling was made of perfectly spiced seekh chicken. The spice level was just right—medium spicy, which added to the overall flavor without overwhelming the palate.

What made it even more special was that it was served on a sizzling plate, enhancing the presentation and aroma. The Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa was a unique addition to the menu, and being the first place to serve it definitely earned them some extra points. The taste was simply amazing, and each bite was a burst of flavor.

I would highly recommend Mao Restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal. The combination of delicious food, unique offerings, and excellent presentation makes it a must-visit spot. Can't wait to go back and try more dishes!

Waited for 15 minutes to get a place.
They serve all sorts of packet Chaknas here like Moong Dal, Chakli, Seng, Chana, Roasted Chana Etc. These are all reasonably priced between 20 to 40.

We order Bombil Fry, Chicken Sukka, Kori Rotti and Neer Dosa & Solkadi
Being married to a Mangalorean and been a regular to Mangalorean outlets back in Kudla I know the taste very well. This was nowhere near sadly. The Bombil Fry being a Maharashtrian special was just oil fried with light red batter rather than Rawa Fry. Killed the appetite completely unfortunately. It was served a small bowl of Coconut gravy which was again very bland.

The Chicken Sukka was too bland. Quantity was ample but the taste was honestly bland. I tried to finish it with the Neer Dosa since Bhakri wasn't available.

Neer Dosa again was served with a small bowl of Coconut gravy as usual bland.

The Kori Rotti being a staple food amongst mangaloreans was a major let down. It didn't have any flavor and even had sasive(Mustard) in it which was unlike of any Mangalorean Outlet. My wife finished it with a lot of difficulty.

The only savior was the Solkadi and it was really tasty and thick. It was too good and cheap at the same time.

Overall verdict is it's a cheap and pocket friendly place. The food was 2/5. Drinks are probably cheap since everyone was busy consuming that. Solkadi 6/5. The staff were always on the feet and ready to attend.

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Just experienced a fantastic meal at the iconic Bharat Excellensea, a 35-year-old gem in Mumbai's Ballard Estate! The restaurant has been recently revamped, and the ambiance is now even more inviting. But the real star is the food!

As a self-proclaimed seafood addict, I was in heaven. I sampled a wide range of dishes, each bursting with flavor and freshness.

The Tom Kha Soup was a fragrant and comforting start. The Prawns Butter Garlic were perfectly cooked and incredibly flavorful. The *Yellow Chili Prawns  packed a delicious spicy punch. The Surmai Masala Fry was a classic done exceptionally well. The Thalasseri Clams were a fiery delight, showcasing the flavors of Kerala. The Rawas Gassi was a rich and creamy Mangalorean-style curry. The Neer Dosa and Appam were the perfect accompaniments to soak up the delicious gravies.

But the real surprise was the Sitaphal Tricones Holige! This innovative dessert was a delightful fusion of Indian and modern flavors. A must-try!

Overall:
Bharat Excellensea is a must-visit for any seafood lover in Mumbai. The restaurant offers a wide variety of fresh, flavorful dishes with influences from across India's coastal regions. The recent revamp has enhanced the dining experience, making it a perfect spot for a special occasion or a memorable meal. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this restaurant on the way to Crawford Market. I’ve been coming here since childhood—not very regularly, but occasionally.I went for kheema pav, but the owner suggested bheja along with kheema pav, so I went with his recommendation.

When the dish arrived, the portion size was quite small and didn’t feel worth ₹240. On top of that, they charge ₹20 extra for pav, which feels a bit excessive. The taste was very good—rich and flavorful—but slightly too spicy and oily for my liking.

In the afternoon, the place is usually packed, especially for non-vegetarian dishes. However, as a local Mumbaikar, I do feel the pricing is on the higher side. Either the cost should be more reasonable or the portion size should be increased to justify it.

The owner was actively moving around, asking customers for feedback and promoting items like fish fry, caramel custard, and solkadhi. While this does help in building customer relationships, a major drawback comes at the time of billing—they do not accept UPI payments, only cash.

featured_reviews.name: Curious Fork
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Feast Worth the Journey from Pune!
We travelled all the way from Pune just to eat at Hotel Grant House, and it was worth every minute. This restaurant has been on our bucket list for a while, and it thoroughly satisfied our hunger. We left full and sent them a lot of blessings for such delicious food!  We were hungry so didn't have the patience to take pictures to post.
The Fried Bombil, Crab Lollipop, Prawns Masala, and Prawns Pulav were outstanding. The river prawns were sweet and cooked perfectly.Mutton Khima was flavourful, well-spiced, and delicious. Their last portion of caramel custard had our name on it, so glad! That was so good too.
The staff is incredibly polite and attentive. A special thanks to the manager, Shridhar, who suggested a few items every single recommendation was spot on and scrumptious.
The restaurant is located in a crowded area and the street is not well lit but the food is so good that the surroundings do not matter. It is a definitive must-try place if you are in the area. We only wish they had a branch in Pune!

featured_reviews.name: Debabrata Golder
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are a seafood lover looking for an authentic and budget-friendly meal near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CST), Sandeep Gomantak Hotel is an absolute must-visit.
Getting There & Parking
The restaurant is incredibly convenient if you are traveling by train, located just a short 5 to 7-minute walk from the CST station. I highly recommend that you go by walk only. Because it is situated in a bustling, crowded area, there is absolutely no parking available. Trying to find a spot for your vehicle nearby is a major problem and will only add unnecessary hassle to your meal, so walking is definitely the smartest option.
Ambiance & Service
Despite being a busy eatery, the management does a great job of maintaining the space. The dining area is kept very neat and clean, making for a comfortable environment to enjoy your meal. Additionally, the service is impressively fast. The staff is efficient and attentive, ensuring you get your food quickly even during peak lunch or dinner hours.
The Food
The star of the show here is undoubtedly the authentic Konkan-style cooking. The fish items are perfectly spiced, incredibly fresh, and exceptionally tasty. What makes it even better is that everything is well under budget, offering fantastic value for money without compromising on flavor. If you visit, you absolutely must try the crab—it is wonderfully prepared and easily one of the standout dishes on the menu.
Verdict
Overall, Sandeep Gomantak offers a fantastic, no-frills dining experience that hits all the right notes for coastal food cravings. Fast service, clean surroundings, and mouth-watering seafood make it a true hidden gem. Highly recommended!
